assumptions: Priya arrived from a Google search for 'milestone birthday' on her phone, with her own 30th coming up.
She reads the intro, Key takeaways, skims the ideas list and the 30th section, glances at the FAQ, then leaves or bookmarks.
HTML comments, image slot notes and fact markers are invisible to her.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya (search visitor, phone, does not know the brand)
No invented brand facts; missing information listed in unanswered_questions
Every suggested edit 'old' is an exact, unique substring of 05-draft.md
No suggested edit adds prices, fees, commissions, vendor names, statistics, em dashes or business details
Did not invent problems; positives recorded where the draft works

open_questions.question: Will the published page show a 'last updated' date? As a search visitor I look for one to judge if the advice is current; this is a template question, not a copy edit.

first_impression.reaction: Good, the first line actually answers what a milestone birthday is and the Key takeaways are right there. No fluff wall before it. I kept going to see the ideas.

journey.quote: A milestone birthday marks a new decade or an age that feels significant: the 30th, 40th, 50th, 60th and beyond.
journey.reaction: Straight answer in the first sentence. That's what I came for.

journey.quote: Settle the guest list and your priorities before you look at dates or venues, because both shape every decision that follows.
journey.reaction: Useful and quick. Four bullets I can read between stops.

journey.section: What makes a birthday a milestone
journey.quote: A milestone birthday closes a decade or marks an age the person sees as a turning point.
journey.reaction: This basically repeats the intro. I'd scroll past it.

journey.quote: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby, so keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper, and use sturdy holders made of material that cannot burn, as the [SA Metropolitan Fire Service candle fact sheet](https://www.mfs.sa.gov.au/community-safety/safety-and-education/fact-sheets/candles2/mfs-fact-sheet-candles.pdf) sets out.
journey.reaction: I wanted dinner ideas and got a fire safety lecture longer than the idea itself. On a phone this is a big block of text.

journey.section: A long lunch or garden party
journey.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours.
journey.reaction: I know how sunscreen works. And the UV bit is all about Australia, which doesn't help me in Singapore.

journey.quote: A full surprise suits someone who loves an audience. For anyone who doesn't, a partial surprise is kinder: they know there is a dinner, but not who has flown in for it.
journey.reaction: Nice, practical, short. This is the kind of thing I'd screenshot.

journey.quote: Friends lead the guest list and the night can run late. Give those with young children or little leave plenty of notice.
journey.reaction: This is my one. It's a bit thin for me, but the link to the by-decade ideas is exactly my next click.

journey.section: A party at home or a destination weekend
journey.quote: There is a middle path too: a party at home for the wider circle, then a few days away with the closest few.
journey.reaction: The table plus this line is genuinely helpful. Easy to scan.

journey.section: Where everyone stays and one hosted dinner
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans milestone birthdays through the same Wedded Advisor process: one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, working in your time zone and quoting in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: Wait, this is a wedding site? 'Couples' feels off when I'm planning my own birthday. And 'the same Wedded Advisor process' means nothing to me, I've never heard of it.

journey.quote: The birthdays that mark a new decade, along with any age the person sees as a turning point.
journey.reaction: The question asks which ones, so name them. The intro did, the FAQ answer is vaguer than the intro.

journey.quote: Neither is better. A party gathers everyone in one room, while a trip gives a smaller group real time together. Some hosts do both.
journey.reaction: Honest answer, no sales pitch. Good.

unanswered_questions: When was this written or last updated? Is it still current for 2026?
Roughly what does each format cost to throw (a dinner versus a weekend away)? I'm not asking the page to add numbers, just noting I'd still have to look elsewhere.
What actually is Wedded Concierge, and does it help people outside Australia like me in Singapore?

turn_offs_found.quote: A candle is an open flame and can easily ignite anything combustible nearby, so keep the area around each one clear of linen, florals and paper
turn_offs_found.why: Safety detail is longer than the idea it sits under. Slows the scan on a phone.

turn_offs_found.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before going outside and again every two hours.
turn_offs_found.why: Obvious advice that pads out the section. Feels like filler.

turn_offs_found.quote: quoting in AUD for Australian couples
turn_offs_found.why: 'Couples' on a birthday article makes the brand feel like it copy-pasted from a wedding page.

would_share_with: A friend helping plan my 30th (the ideas list and home vs destination table)

cta_reaction.why: I came for ideas, not a planner, and I still don't know what this service is. I might bookmark the page, but I'm not enquiring from a train.

top_3_changes: Cut the candle safety paragraph down so the dinner idea stays the focus.
Name the milestone ages in the FAQ answer instead of being vaguer than the intro.
Change 'Australian couples' to a word that fits a birthday host.
